args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks following the production deploy of v2.3.1. At detection, all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) were on v2.3.1 with service health reported unhealthy and an error rate of ~18%.

Remediation: initiated a rollback to v2.3.0, the most recent version with a healthy production record (v2.3.1's prior staging release, v2.3.1-rc, also showed unhealthy). The first rollback attempt returned a partial_failure ("Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error") and left the fleet in a mixed state — us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west remained on the unhealthy v2.3.1. A retry of the rollback to v2.3.0 completed successfully across all regions.

Current status: v2.3.0 running in us-east, us-west, and eu-west. Service health is reported healthy and error rate has dropped to ~0.2%.

Follow-up needed: root-cause analysis on why v2.3.1 failed health checks, and why the initial rollback halted mid-rollout with an orchestrator error. v2.3.1 should not be redeployed to production until the failure is understood and it has demonstrated health in a lower environment.

Done — no retry needed; the incident was created despite the client-side timeout.

## Summary

**Diagnosis:** `checkout-api` was on v2.3.1 in all three production regions, failing health checks with an ~18% error rate.

**Target version:** v2.3.0 — the most recent release with a healthy production record. Note that v2.3.1's only other artifact, v2.3.1-rc, was also unhealthy in staging, so there was no ambiguity about v2.3.1 being the bad release.

**Rollback (took two attempts):**
1. First attempt returned `partial_failure: "Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error"`. I verified actual state rather than assuming: this left the fleet in a **mixed state** — us-east on v2.3.0, but us-west and eu-west still on the unhealthy v2.3.1.
2. Retried the rollback to v2.3.0, which completed across all regions.

**Verified result:** v2.3.0 in us-east, us-west, and eu-west. Service healthy, error rate down to ~0.2%.

**Incident:** INC-0001, SEV2, open. My `create_incident` call timed out at 30s, so I checked `list_incidents` before retrying and confirmed it had actually gone through — avoiding a duplicate page to on-call.

**Two things worth flagging for the follow-up:**
- The mid-rollout orchestrator error is a separate reliability concern from the bad deploy. A rollback that halts leaving production split across two versions is arguably worse than the original failure mode, so that deserves its own investigation rather than being lumped in with the v2.3.1 RCA.
- v2.3.1 should not return to production until it's understood and has proven healthy in a lower environment. That would require change-manager approval under the platform policy, since v2.3.1 has never been healthy in production.
